intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, spices, and cured meats. Sample street food like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A guided walking food tour enhances the experience with cultural context.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania focused on authentic Cretan cuisine, one of the healthiest diets in the world. Learn to prepare dishes like dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and honey-drizzled kalitsounia pastries using locally sourced ingredients. Classes typically include a market visit and a full meal.

experiences.name: Mykonos Beach Club & Local Taverna Evening
experiences.description: Spend the afternoon at Paradise Beach or Psarou Beach on Mykonos, enjoying the golden sand and clear blue waters. As the sun sets, head to a local taverna in Mykonos Town (Chora) for a traditional Greek dinner featuring fresh grilled octopus, tzatziki, fresh-caught fish, and local Assyrtiko wine at a fraction of the beach club prices.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from street level. Grab a souvlaki wrap from a street vendor to kick off your Greek food experience.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros or tiropita (cheese pie) from a bakery near the airport or on arrival
meals.dinner: Street souvlaki wrap with tzatziki from a Monastiraki street stall — around €2–3

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 14:50 arrival. Book accommodation in advance in Monastiraki, Psiri, or Omonia for best budget value. Metro Line 3 from airport to Monastiraki costs ~€9.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket (~€20) includes entry to several other ancient sites valid for 5 days — great value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (covered by the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus. Afterward, browse the colorful Monastiraki Flea Market for affordable souvenirs and local goods.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Thisio neighborhood for sunset views of the Acropolis from the pedestrian promenade. Enjoy dinner at a local taverna in Psiri.

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and Greek coffee from a local bakery — ~€3
meals.lunch: Cheap gyros plate at a Monastiraki eatery — ~€5–7
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Psiri — try moussaka or pastitsio with house wine — ~€10–12

day_by_day.notes: Buy the 5-day combined Acropolis ticket (€20) — it covers the Agora, Roman Agora, Kerameikos, and more. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum (one of the world's great museums, entry ~€10). Spend 2–3 hours exploring ancient Greek artifacts, sculptures, and the Antikythera Mechanism.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Exarchia neighborhood — Athens' bohemian quarter with street art, independent cafes, and a lively local vibe. Visit the Strefi Hill park for free panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Take the tram or bus to the coastal suburb of Faliro for a free beach walk along the waterfront promenade. Enjoy fresh seafood at a budget fish taverna.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts at a café near the museum — ~€4
meals.lunch: Souvlaki and fries at a local grill in Exarchia — ~€5
meals.dinner: Grilled sardines and salad at a seaside taverna in Faliro — ~€10–12

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Tuesdays — plan accordingly. Exarchia is safe during the day and great for authentic local atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early ferry from Piraeus port to the island of Aegina (about 1 hour, ~€8–10 each way). Rent a bicycle on arrival (~€5/day) and ride to the stunning Temple of Aphaia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or take a local bus to Aegina Town beach for a swim in the clear Saronic Gulf waters. Aegina is famous for its pistachios — buy a bag from a local vendor for a cheap, delicious snack.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Piraeus in the late afternoon/early evening. Head back to Athens and enjoy a quiet dinner near your hostel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri (sesame bread ring) and coffee at Piraeus port before boarding — ~€2
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or octopus at a waterfront taverna in Aegina Town — ~€10
meals.dinner: Simple Greek salad and bread with olive oil at a neighborhood taverna in Athens — ~€7–8

day_by_day.notes: Ferries from Piraeus to Aegina run frequently. Take Metro Line 1 from Monastiraki to Piraeus (~€1.20). Aegina is a perfect budget day trip — affordable and less touristy than the Cyclades.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early KTEL bus from Athens to Nafplio (~2.5 hours, ~€13). Explore the charming old town with its Venetian architecture, neoclassical mansions, and narrow cobblestone streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb the 999 steps to the impressive Palamidi Fortress (entry ~€4) for sweeping views over the Argolic Gulf. Afterward, cool off with a swim at Arvanitia beach, a small rocky cove just below the old town walls — free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Nafplio waterfront promenade at sunset. Enjoy dinner at a local taverna in the old town before taking the evening bus back to Athens or staying overnight in a budget guesthouse.

meals.breakfast: On the bus or grab a pastry at the Athens bus terminal — ~€2
meals.lunch: Souvlaki or a cheap gyros plate in Nafplio old town — ~€5–6
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood mezedes (small plates) at a waterfront taverna — ~€12–14

day_by_day.notes: KTEL buses depart from Athens' Kifissos terminal. Consider staying overnight in Nafplio to save time and explore more — budget guesthouses available from €25–35/night.

day_by_day.morning: If staying in Nafplio, take a morning bus to Epidaurus (~30 min, ~€3) to visit the ancient Theatre of Epidaurus — one of the best-preserved ancient theatres in the world (entry ~€12). Test the famous acoustics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Athens by afternoon bus. Check into accommodation and freshen up. Visit the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) on Athinas Street — a vibrant, authentic food market with fresh produce, meat, fish, and spices.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Koukaki neighborhood south of the Acropolis — a trendy, local area with affordable restaurants and bars. Enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and tiropita at a Nafplio bakery — ~€3
meals.lunch: Cheap eats at the Central Market area — try a bowl of bean soup (fasolada) at a traditional eatery — ~€5
meals.dinner: Mezedes platter (hummus, taramosalata, dolmades) with pita at a Koukaki taverna — ~€10

day_by_day.notes: The Epidaurus theatre hosts summer festival performances (June–August) — check the Hellenic Festival website for budget tickets if interested in an evening show.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Piraeus to Hydra island (~2 hours by Flying Dolphin hydrofoil, ~€25–30 each way). Hydra is car-free — donkeys and boats are the only transport. Walk up to the hilltop monastery for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at Vlychos or Kamini beach — small, scenic coves accessible by a 30-minute walk or a short water taxi (~€5). The water is crystal clear and perfect for snorkeling.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the Hydra harbor before catching the return hydrofoil to Piraeus. Hydra's harbor at dusk is magical and free to enjoy.

meals.breakfast: Grab coffee and a pastry at Piraeus before boarding — ~€3
meals.lunch: Grilled octopus and Greek salad at a harbor taverna in Hydra — ~€12–14
meals.dinner: Back in Athens — cheap souvlaki or a gyros wrap near your hostel — ~€4

day_by_day.notes: Hydra is slightly pricier than other islands due to its exclusivity, but day-tripping keeps costs manageable. Bring cash as ATMs can have queues. Wear good walking shoes — the island is hilly.

day_by_day.morning: Take an overnight or early morning ferry/flight to Santorini (ferry from Piraeus ~8 hours, ~€35–50 in economy deck seating — book in advance). Arrive and check into a budget hostel in Fira or Perissa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Perissa Black Sand Beach on the south coast — one of Santorini's most accessible and budget-friendly beaches. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the dramatic volcanic landscape. Sun loungers available cheaply or bring your own towel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Fira town on foot — browse the clifftop walkway with caldera views. Watch the famous Santorini sunset (free!) from the Fira caldera path or the less-crowded Imerovigli viewpoint.

meals.breakfast: On the ferry or grab a pastry upon arrival — ~€3
meals.lunch: Gyros or souvlaki at a Perissa beach snack bar — ~€5–6
meals.dinner: Fresh fish or grilled meat at a budget taverna in Fira — ~€12–15

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets well in advance for June travel. Economy deck seating is the cheapest option. Santorini is more expensive than Athens — budget €40–60/day for food, transport, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the famous Fira to Oia trail (~10 km, 3–4 hours) along the caldera rim — completely free and one of the most scenic walks in Greece. Pass through Firostefani and Imerovigli with stunning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Oia and explore the iconic blue-domed churches and whitewashed alleys. Visit the Oia Castle ruins for caldera views. Take the local bus back to Fira (~€1.80) to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Perissa or Kamari beach for a relaxed evening swim as the day cools. Enjoy dinner at a local taverna near your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and fruit at a Fira café before the hike — ~€4
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a Fira supermarket for the hike — bread, cheese, olives, tomatoes — ~€5
meals.dinner: Grilled lamb chops or fresh calamari at a Perissa taverna — ~€12

day_by_day.notes: Start the Fira–Oia hike early (before 9 AM) to avoid midday heat. Bring 2 liters of water, sunscreen, and a hat. The trail is well-marked but can be rocky in places.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus to Akrotiri (~€2) to visit the prehistoric Minoan settlement — often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean' (entry ~€12). Remarkably preserved ruins buried by the volcanic eruption of 1600 BC.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes from Akrotiri to the Red Beach — one of Santorini's most dramatic and unique beaches with towering red volcanic cliffs. Free entry, bring your own gear.
day_by_day.evening: Take the ferry from Santorini to Mykonos (approximately 2–3 hours, ~€25–35 economy). Arrive in Mykonos and check into a budget hostel in Mykonos Town (Chora).

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita and coffee from a Fira bakery — ~€3
meals.lunch: Cheap gyros or a sandwich near Akrotiri — ~€5
meals.dinner: On the ferry or grab a quick bite upon arrival in Mykonos — ~€6–8

day_by_day.notes: Red Beach requires a short rocky walk from the parking area — wear sturdy sandals. Book the Santorini–Mykonos ferry in advance. Mykonos is expensive — budget accommodation fills up fast in June.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Mykonos Town (Chora) on foot — wander through the iconic whitewashed labyrinthine alleys, visit the famous windmills at Kato Mili, and stroll through Little Venice waterfront. All free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus (~€2) to Paradise Beach or Paraga Beach — two of Mykonos' most popular beaches. Swim in the turquoise Aegean waters. Avoid the expensive beach clubs and find a free spot on the sand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for the evening. Explore the local food market and pick up supplies. Enjoy a budget dinner at a local gyros shop — Mykonos has several affordable options away from the tourist strip.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and koulouri from a local bakery in Chora — ~€3
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach — supermarket supplies (cheese, bread, fruit, water) — ~€6
meals.dinner: Gyros wrap or souvlaki at a local grill in Chora — ~€5–7

day_by_day.notes: Mykonos is one of Greece's most expensive islands. Save money by self-catering for some meals, using local buses instead of taxis, and avoiding the famous beach clubs. Stay in a hostel dorm for best value.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short boat trip from Mykonos Old Port to the sacred island of Delos (~30 min, ~€20 round trip including entry). Explore one of the most important archaeological sites in Greece — the birthplace of Apollo and Artemis.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon at Agios Sostis beach — a quieter, less commercialized beach on the north coast accessible by local bus or a 30-minute walk. No beach clubs, just natural beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Mykonos — enjoy a sunset walk along the Little Venice waterfront. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner at a mid-range taverna as a farewell to the islands.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait and coffee at a Chora café — ~€5
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Agios Sostis beach — supermarket supplies — ~€5
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish and a glass of local wine at a Mykonos taverna — ~€15–18

day_by_day.notes: Delos boats depart from the Old Port at 9:00 AM and 10:00 AM. The site is exposed with no shade — bring water, sunscreen, and a hat. Delos is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece — take a leisurely walk through Mykonos Town one last time. Visit the local market for last-minute affordable souvenirs: local honey, herbs, olive oil, or small ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry or flight back to Athens (ferry ~4–5 hours economy ~€30, or short flight ~€40–60). If time allows before departure, enjoy one final Greek coffee and pastry at a Piraeus or Athens café.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with wonderful memories. If your return flight is late, store luggage at Athens airport or a central luggage storage facility (~€5–8) and spend remaining hours exploring the Plaka neighborhood one last time.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — fresh bread, feta, olives, tomatoes, and coffee at a Mykonos bakery — ~€5
meals.lunch: Souvlaki wrap or gyros at a Piraeus or Athens eatery — ~€4–5
meals.dinner: Airport meal or final taverna dinner in Athens if time permits — ~€10–12

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry/flight times carefully and allow extra time for port-to-airport transfers. Athens airport is connected by Metro Line 3 (~€9, 40 minutes from city center). Keep some euros for airport snacks and transport.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 via Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens. Check in to your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Plaka neighborhood. Freshen up and take a gentle stroll through the charming Plaka district to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric Monastiraki Flea Market area as the evening crowds gather. Enjoy your first Greek dinner at a traditional taverna in Plaka, soaking in the ambiance of the old city beneath the Acropolis lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap or spanakopita from a street kiosk near the airport or in central Athens after check-in (€4–7)
meals.dinner: Taverna Lysikratous or similar traditional taverna in Plaka — try moussaka, tzatziki, and a Greek salad with local house wine (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. The Metro from the airport to Syntagma takes about 40 minutes and costs €9. Exchange some euros at the airport if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Acropolis (open from 8:00 AM) before the heat and crowds build. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and the Propylaea. Purchase a combined ticket (€30) that also covers several other archaeological sites in Athens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the world-class Acropolis Museum at the base of the hill — it houses stunning original sculptures and artifacts from the Acropolis site. Afterward, walk to the Ancient Agora of Athens, the heart of ancient Greek civic life, and explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the vibrant Monastiraki and Psiri neighborhoods for evening drinks and dinner. Explore the lively squares and rooftop bars with Acropolis views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café near Plaka — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, fresh orange juice, and a freddo espresso (€6–10)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Acropolis Museum café with a view — salads, sandwiches, and mezze platters (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Monastiraki such as Couleur Locale or similar — enjoy grilled octopus, fava dip, and fresh fish with Acropolis views (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sunscreen and a hat. The Acropolis involves significant uphill walking on uneven marble surfaces. Book Acropolis Museum entry online in advance to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum of Athens, one of the greatest museums in the world, housing treasures from across ancient Greece including the Antikythera Mechanism and Mycenaean gold artifacts. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood and walk up Lycabettus Hill (by funicular or on foot) for panoramic 360-degree views over Athens and the Saronic Gulf. Afterward, browse the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) for a sensory immersion into local food culture — olives, spices, fresh fish, and meats.
day_by_day.evening: Take an evening food tour or explore the Exarchia and Kolonaki neighborhoods for dinner. Try a mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) for a social, sharing-style Greek meal.

meals.breakfast: Bakery breakfast near your hotel — tiropita (cheese pie), koulouri (sesame bread ring), and Greek coffee (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Eat at the Central Market area — fresh souvlaki, grilled meats, or a hearty bean soup (fasolada) at a local workers' taverna (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Mezedopoleio in Exarchia or Kolonaki — order a spread of mezedes: dolmades, saganaki, grilled halloumi, taramasalata, and local Assyrtiko wine (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Tuesdays — Wednesday through Monday it opens at 8:00 AM. The Varvakios Market is most lively in the morning; try to visit before 1:00 PM for the best atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens by ferry from Piraeus Port to Santorini (approximately 5–8 hours by standard ferry, or 2 hours by high-speed catamaran). Book the high-speed option for comfort. Enjoy the Aegean Sea views from the deck as you approach the dramatic caldera of Santorini.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Santorini (Thira). Check in to your mid-range hotel in Fira or Firostefani. Take the cable car up from the port to Fira town. Explore the winding whitewashed streets of Fira, browse local shops, and visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the caldera-edge path from Fira toward Firostefani for stunning sunset views over the volcanic caldera. Enjoy dinner at a caldera-view restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Athens hotel before heading to Piraeus (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the ferry or eat at the ferry's onboard café — sandwiches, pastries, and coffee (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range caldera-view restaurant in Fira — try fresh grilled sea bream, Santorinian fava (yellow split pea dip), and local Vinsanto wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets well in advance for June travel — Santorini is extremely popular. The high-speed catamaran (SeaJets or Hellenic Seaways) costs approximately €60–80 one way. Fira is very walkable but has steep steps — pack light for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Rent an ATV or hire a local taxi to explore the island. Visit the iconic village of Oia in the morning before the crowds arrive — wander its blue-domed churches, narrow alleys, and art galleries. Explore the Oia Castle ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kamari Beach or Perissa Beach on the eastern coast — Santorini's famous black volcanic sand beaches. Rent a sunbed and umbrella, swim in the clear Aegean waters, and relax. The black sand gets very hot, so wear sandals.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Oia for the world-famous Santorini sunset — arrive at least an hour early to secure a good viewing spot. The sunset from Oia Castle is legendary. Enjoy dinner in Oia afterward.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café in Fira — Greek yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and freddo cappuccino (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Kamari or Perissa — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold Mythos beer (€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Oia after sunset — try a mid-range restaurant serving Santorinian specialties like white eggplant, cherry tomato fritters, and fresh lobster pasta (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Oia at sunset is extremely crowded in June — arrive by 7:00 PM for a good spot. ATV rental costs approximately €25–35 per day. Perissa Beach has more budget-friendly tavernas than Kamari. Wear reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning volcano and hot springs boat tour from Fira's old port (Ammoudi Bay). Visit the active Nea Kameni volcanic island, hike to the crater, and swim in the natural sulfuric hot springs. A truly unique Santorini experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient ruins of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by the volcanic eruption around 1600 BC, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' The site is covered and air-conditioned, perfect for the afternoon heat.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed final evening in Santorini. Explore the local wine scene — visit a winery such as Santo Wines or Domaine Sigalas for a tasting of indigenous Assyrtiko and Nykteri wines with caldera views.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the boat tour — pastries and coffee from a local bakery in Fira (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Lunch back in Fira after the tour — try a local gyros shop or a casual mezedopoleio (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Wine and mezedes dinner at Santo Wines winery or a nearby restaurant — cheese platters, cured meats, and local wines (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The volcano boat tour costs approximately €20–25 per person and departs multiple times daily from the old port. Book Akrotiri tickets online (€12 entry). The winery visit is a great way to spend a relaxed Sunday evening — Santo Wines has spectacular sunset views.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Santorini to Zakynthos (via Athens or direct seasonal routes — check schedules). Alternatively, fly from Santorini to Zakynthos via Athens (approximately 2–3 hours total with connection). Check in to your mid-range hotel in Zakynthos Town or Laganas area.
day_by_day.afternoon: After arriving and settling in, visit Zakynthos Town (Chora) — explore the Venetian-influenced architecture, the Byzantine Museum, and the main Solomos Square. Walk along the harbor promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed first evening in Zakynthos. Explore the local tavernas along the harbor for fresh Ionian seafood.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Santorini hotel before departure (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Airport or ferry snacks, or a quick meal upon arrival in Zakynthos (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Harborside taverna in Zakynthos Town — try fresh grilled octopus, bourdeto (spicy fish stew), and local Verdea white wine (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Inter-island travel in Greece can be complex — flying via Athens is often the most reliable option. Book flights or ferries well in advance. The journey may take most of the morning and early afternoon depending on connections. Zakynthos is in the Ionian Sea, west of mainland Greece.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat tour to the iconic **Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach)** — one of Greece's most photographed and spectacular beaches. The only way to reach it is by boat from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town. The turquoise water enclosed by towering white limestone cliffs is absolutely breathtaking. Swim and explore the famous rusting shipwreck on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat tour to the Blue Caves on the northern tip of Zakynthos — sea caves where the water glows an ethereal electric blue due to light refraction. Swim inside the caves for an unforgettable experience. Return to your hotel by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and enjoy the sunset from a clifftop viewpoint above Navagio Beach (accessible by road) for a different perspective. Dinner in a local village taverna.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café — Greek yogurt, honey, fresh fruit, and coffee (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for the boat tour, or eat at a small beach café near Porto Vromi before/after the tour (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Traditional village taverna in Anafonitria or Volimes — try sofrito (veal in white wine sauce), fresh grilled fish, and local wine (€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Navagio Beach boat tour costs approximately €15–25 per person depending on the operator. Tours typically depart in the morning. Bring waterproof sunscreen, a towel, and water shoes. The beach has no shade — the cliffs provide some relief. Book the boat tour the day before to secure a spot.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Laganas Beach and the surrounding area — Zakynthos is home to one of the most important loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) nesting sites in the Mediterranean. Take a responsible sea turtle watching boat tour in the morning to spot these magnificent creatures in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the inland villages of Zakynthos — visit Machairado with its beautiful church, and the village of Keri for its lighthouse and dramatic clifftop views over the Ionian Sea. Stop at local honey and olive oil producers along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zakynthos Town for a final evening on the island. Visit the Venetian Castle above the town for panoramic views, then enjoy a leisurely dinner.

meals.breakfast: Bakery breakfast in Laganas — tiropita, spanakopita, and Greek coffee (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a village café in Keri or Machairado — simple Greek salad, grilled meats, and local bread (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Zakynthos Town — try mandolato (local nougat) for dessert and sample local Zakynthian cuisine (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sea turtle watching tours must be conducted responsibly — choose operators certified by the Sea Turtle Protection Society of Greece (ARCHELON). Do not touch or disturb the turtles. Laganas Bay is a protected National Marine Park.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Zakynthos to Heraklion, Crete (via Athens if necessary — approximately 2–3 hours total). Check in to your mid-range hotel in Heraklion or Chania. If arriving in Heraklion, visit the impressive Heraklion Archaeological Museum, home to the world's finest collection of Minoan art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palace of Knossos — the legendary Bronze Age palace of the Minoan civilization, associated with the myth of the Minotaur and the Labyrinth. Explore the remarkably reconstructed ruins with a local guide for context.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Heraklion's vibrant old town — walk along the Venetian harbor, visit the Koules Fortress, and browse the lively market street (1866 Street) for local products.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Zakynthos hotel before departure (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near Knossos — local taverna serving Cretan specialties like dakos (barley rusk salad) and grilled lamb (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional Cretan restaurant in Heraklion old town — try lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), Cretan cheese, and local Vidiano wine (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Knossos entry costs €15 (or €20 with the Archaeological Museum combined ticket). A guided tour is highly recommended to understand the site's complex history. Crete is Greece's largest island with a distinct culinary tradition — embrace the local Cretan diet, considered one of the healthiest in the world.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning drive or bus to **Elafonissi Beach** in southwestern Crete — one of Greece's most stunning beaches, famous for its pink-tinged sand (colored by crushed coral and shells) and shallow, crystal-clear turquoise lagoon. The drive takes approximately 1.5–2 hours from Heraklion or 1 hour from Chania.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Elafonissi — swim in the shallow lagoon, walk across the sandbar to the small island of Elafonissi, explore the dunes, and relax on the pink sand. The water is exceptionally clear and calm, making it ideal for snorkeling.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Chania (if basing yourself there) or Heraklion. Stop in the charming old Venetian town of Chania for dinner — one of Crete's most beautiful cities with a stunning harbor.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — Cretan honey, fresh bread, and local cheese at your hotel or a roadside café (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna near Elafonissi — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold drinks (€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Chania Venetian harbor — try fresh seafood, Cretan lamb, and local raki (Cretan spirit) at a harborside restaurant (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is very popular in June — arrive early (before 10:00 AM) to secure a good spot and avoid the worst of the crowds. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and snorkeling gear. The beach has limited shade. Car rental in Crete costs approximately €30–50 per day and is highly recommended for flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the famous Samaria Gorge — one of Europe's longest gorges at 16 km, cutting through the White Mountains (Lefka Ori) of western Crete. The hike takes 4–6 hours and ends at the coastal village of Agia Roumeli. The scenery is spectacular with towering rock walls, wildflowers, and mountain streams.
day_by_day.afternoon: Upon completing the gorge hike, arrive at Agia Roumeli beach — a remote, pristine beach accessible only by boat or on foot. Take a refreshing swim in the Libyan Sea to cool down after the hike. Take the ferry from Agia Roumeli to Hora Sfakion (approximately 1 hour), then bus or taxi back to your base.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania or Heraklion. Enjoy a well-deserved relaxing dinner celebrating your gorge achievement. Explore the evening atmosphere of Chania's old town.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast before the gorge — energy-rich foods: eggs, bread, cheese, and fruit (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch for the gorge — energy bars, nuts, fruit, and plenty of water (prepare the night before)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a Cretan taverna — slow-roasted lamb (kleftiko), horta (wild greens), and a carafe of local wine (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Samaria Gorge is open from May to October. Entry fee is €5. Wear sturdy hiking shoes — the terrain is rocky. Bring at least 2 liters of water per person, sunscreen, and a light jacket for the cool gorge interior. The total journey (gorge + ferry + bus) takes a full day. Book the return ferry in advance during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Crete — visit the Chania Municipal Market (Agora) for a last immersion in Greek food culture. Stock up on local products to take home: Cretan olive oil, thyme honey, dried herbs, local cheeses (graviera, anthotyros), and Cretan rusks. Browse the stalls and chat with local vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final swim at a nearby beach — Falasarna Beach near Chania is one of Crete's finest, with golden sand and clear water. Alternatively, take a final stroll through Chania's old town, visit the Maritime Museum, and enjoy a last coffee at a harborside café.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Heraklion or Chania airport for your return flight. Reflect on 13 incredible days exploring Greece's beaches, ancient history, and extraordinary food culture.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at a Chania café — full spread of local cheeses, olives, honey, yogurt, and coffee (€10–14)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach taverna at Falasarna or a café in Chania old town — dakos salad, fresh juice, and a last gyros (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or an early dinner before departure — or pack some local pastries and snacks from the market for the journey home (€8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Heraklion Airport (HER) and Chania Airport (CHQ) are both well-connected. Liquid restrictions apply for olive oil and wine in carry-on luggage — pack these in checked baggage. Keep your combined Athens archaeological site ticket as a wonderful souvenir.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, spices, and cured meats. Sample street food like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A guided walking food tour enhances the experience with cultural context.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania focused on authentic Cretan cuisine, one of the healthiest diets in the world. Learn to prepare dishes like dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and honey-drizzled kalitsounia pastries using locally sourced ingredients. Classes typically include a market visit and a full meal.

experiences.name: Mykonos Beach Club & Local Taverna Evening
experiences.description: Spend the afternoon at Paradise Beach or Psarou Beach on Mykonos, enjoying the golden sand and clear blue waters. As the sun sets, head to a local taverna in Mykonos Town (Chora) for a traditional Greek dinner featuring fresh grilled octopus, tzatziki, fresh-caught fish, and local Assyrtiko wine at a fraction of the beach club prices.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 via Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your 5-star hotel in Athens (recommended: Hotel Grande Bretagne or Electra Metropolis). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink at the rooftop bar overlooking the Acropolis.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle evening stroll through the Plaka neighborhood — Athens' oldest district with charming neoclassical architecture, bougainvillea-draped alleys, and views of the illuminated Acropolis. Settle in at a premium taverna for your first taste of Greek cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Served on the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack at the airport or in-flight
meals.dinner: Dinner at Strofi Restaurant (Rovertou Galli 25, Makrigianni) — a legendary Athens taverna with panoramic Acropolis views, renowned for traditional Greek mezedes, grilled octopus, and lamb chops. Reserve a terrace table in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer is strongly recommended for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm hotel concierge services upon check-in for upcoming day trips and restaurant reservations throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour — Begin your morning at the legendary Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) for an immersive guided food tour. Explore stalls overflowing with fresh fish, cured meats, olives, spices, and artisan cheeses. Sample local delicacies including loukoumades (honey doughnuts), taramosalata, and aged graviera cheese. Your expert guide will share stories of Athenian culinary heritage and help you source premium Greek products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis and Acropolis Museum with a private guide. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea at a leisurely premium pace (skip-the-line tickets essential). Follow with a curated visit to the world-class Acropolis Museum, where ancient artifacts are displayed with stunning views of the hill itself.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar of your hotel or at A for Athens rooftop bar in Monastiraki, offering breathtaking Acropolis panoramas. Then head to dinner at a refined modern Greek restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast buffet featuring Greek yogurt with Cretan honey, fresh pastries, smoked salmon, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: During the food tour — curated tastings at the Central Market including fresh bread, olives, cheeses, and cured meats count as a gourmet lunch experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at Varoulko Seaside (Akti Koumoundourou 52, Piraeus) — Michelin-starred seafood restaurant by chef Lefteris Lazarou, celebrated for creative Greek seafood cuisine. Private taxi transfer recommended (20 min from central Athens).

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis skip-the-line tickets and private guide at least 2 weeks in advance. The Central Market food tour is best experienced early morning (8:00–10:30) when the market is at its most vibrant.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the ancient Agora of Athens and Hephaestus Temple — one of the best-preserved ancient Greek temples in the world. Wander through the archaeological site with an audio guide or private historian. Afterward, browse the upscale boutiques and galleries of Kolonaki neighborhood, Athens' most fashionable district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Archaeological Museum — the largest archaeological museum in Greece, housing treasures including the Antikythera Mechanism, Mycenaean gold masks, and stunning Cycladic figurines. Take your time in the premium air-conditioned galleries. Late afternoon: relax at your hotel's spa or pool.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Psyrri and Monastiraki neighborhoods for an authentic Athenian evening atmosphere. Enjoy an aperitif at a stylish wine bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit a premium Athenian café — try Tailor Made (Plateia Agias Irinis) for specialty coffee and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Avocado Athens (Nikis 30) — a sophisticated plant-forward restaurant near Syntagma Square, or Tzitzikas & Mermingas for elevated traditional Greek mezedes
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hytra Restaurant (Onassis Cultural Centre, Syngrou 107) — a Michelin-starred modern Greek restaurant offering a tasting menu that reimagines classic Greek flavors with contemporary technique

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Mondays — verify opening hours. Consider booking a private evening Athens food walk through Psyrri for an additional culinary experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Athens International Airport for an early domestic flight to Heraklion, Crete (approximately 55 minutes). Upon arrival, transfer via luxury rental car or private driver to Chania — a 2.5-hour scenic drive along the northern Cretan coast. Check in to your luxury boutique hotel in Chania (recommended: Casa Delfino or Domes of Elounda if budget allows the eastern coast).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the enchanting Venetian Harbor of Chania — stroll along the waterfront promenade, admire the iconic lighthouse, and wander through the narrow lanes of the old town with its Venetian and Ottoman architecture. Visit the covered market (Agora) of Chania for a preview of Cretan produce.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the Venetian Lighthouse followed by a leisurely evening in the old harbor area.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before airport transfer, or grab a premium coffee and tiropita (cheese pie) at the airport
meals.lunch: Upon arrival in Chania — lunch at Tamam Restaurant (Zambeliou 49) housed in a converted Ottoman bathhouse, serving creative Cretan-Mediterranean cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Thalassino Ageri (Vivilaki 35, Chania) — an acclaimed seafood restaurant perched above the sea, offering the freshest Cretan catch with exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flights well in advance. Alternatively, a ferry from Piraeus to Heraklion overnight (luxury cabin) is a romantic option if you prefer not to fly. Confirm hotel check-in time given afternoon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class — Join a hands-on premium cooking class in Chania focused on authentic Cretan cuisine, widely regarded as one of the healthiest diets in the world. Learn to prepare dishes such as dakos (Cretan rusk salad), spanakopita, slow-cooked lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and loukoumades. Classes typically take place in a traditional farmhouse or olive grove setting with a local chef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Archaeological Museum of Chania and the Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Collection. Then explore the leather-goods workshops and artisan shops of Skrydlof Street (Leather Lane). Late afternoon: relax at your hotel or take a dip at a nearby beach.
day_by_day.evening: Evening walk through the illuminated Venetian harbor and old town alleyways.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Cretan style with local honey, thyme-infused yogurt, fresh bread, and olive oil
meals.lunch: Included as part of the cooking class experience — you eat what you cook, accompanied by local Cretan wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Portes Restaurant (Portou 48, Chania Old Town) — intimate, romantic setting in a restored Venetian building, serving refined Cretan dishes with an excellent selection of local wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least one week in advance. Classes are typically limited to 8–10 participants for an intimate experience. Request a class that includes a morning visit to a local market for ingredient sourcing.

day_by_day.morning: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip — Depart early by private car (approximately 1.5 hours from Chania) to the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete. Famous for its unique pink-tinged sand (created by crushed coral and shells) and shallow turquoise lagoon, this is one of Greece's most spectacular beaches. Arrive early to secure the best spot before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Elafonissi — wade through the shallow lagoon to the small island, snorkel in the crystal-clear waters, and relax on the pink sand. The water temperature in June is perfect (around 22–24°C). Depart around 16:00 for the return drive to Chania.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Chania — browse the artisan shops and galleries of the old town.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Pack a premium picnic prepared by your hotel, or dine at the beach taverna at Elafonissi (Elafonissi Taverna) — simple but fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold Mythos beer
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ela Restaurant (Kondylaki 47, Chania) — a beloved local institution in a charming courtyard, serving traditional Cretan recipes passed down through generations

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is a protected nature reserve — no umbrellas or sunbeds are available, so bring your own beach mat, umbrella, and snorkeling gear. Apply reef-safe sunscreen. The drive passes through the stunning White Mountains (Lefka Ori) — allow time for photo stops.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Chania by private car to Heraklion Airport (2.5 hours) for a short domestic flight to Mykonos (via Athens if necessary). Alternatively, take a high-speed ferry from Heraklion to Mykonos (approximately 3.5–4 hours on a premium fast ferry). Check in to your luxury hotel in Mykonos (recommended: Cavo Tagoo, Katikies Mykonos, or Bill & Coo Suites).
day_by_day.afternoon: Mykonos Beach Club & Local Taverna Experience — Head to Psarou Beach or Paradise Beach for an afternoon of premium beach club luxury. Psarou Beach is Mykonos' most exclusive beach, frequented by celebrities, with premium sunbed service, cocktails, and crystal-clear Aegean waters. Enjoy the golden sand, swim in the turquoise sea, and soak up the iconic Cycladic atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the iconic Mykonos Town (Chora) — wander through the dazzling white-washed labyrinthine streets, visit the famous windmills at Kato Mili, and watch the sunset from Little Venice (Alefkandra) with a cocktail in hand.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a coffee and fresh koulouri at a Chania bakery before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at the beach club at Psarou Beach — fresh seafood, lobster pasta, and premium cocktails with your feet in the sand
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nobu Matsuhisa Mykonos (Psarou Beach) or Spilia Seaside Restaurant (Kalafatis) — a dramatic cave-set seafood restaurant carved into the cliffs, offering exceptional fresh fish and Aegean views

day_by_day.notes: Book beach club sunbeds at Psarou Beach well in advance — they sell out quickly in June. The ferry option is scenic and luxurious on a high-speed vessel; book premium cabin seats. Confirm hotel transfer from the port or airport.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat tour of Mykonos — Charter a private speedboat or sailing yacht for a morning exploration of Mykonos' hidden sea caves, secluded coves, and pristine beaches inaccessible by land. Swim in secret bays, snorkel over Posidonia seagrass meadows, and enjoy the freedom of the open Aegean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos Town for an afternoon of luxury shopping — browse high-end boutiques, local jewelry designers (Mykonos is famous for its gold jewelry), and artisan ceramics shops. Visit the Folklore Museum and the Archaeological Museum of Mykonos for cultural context.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a cliffside bar in Little Venice — the most iconic sunset spot in the Cyclades. Then enjoy a premium dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast with fresh fruit, Greek yogurt, eggs Benedict, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Onboard the private boat — arrange a catered lunch with your charter company featuring fresh seafood, local cheeses, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Interni Restaurant (Matogianni Street, Mykonos Town) — one of Mykonos' most celebrated fine dining venues set in a stunning garden, offering Mediterranean cuisine with exceptional presentation and an award-winning wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Private boat charters can be arranged through your hotel concierge. Half-day charters (4–5 hours) typically cost €400–€800 depending on vessel size. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light cover-up for the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the sacred island of Delos — take the short ferry from Mykonos Town (30 minutes) to one of the most important archaeological sites in the entire Mediterranean. Delos was the mythological birthplace of Apollo and Artemis and was the commercial hub of the ancient Greek world. Explore the Terrace of the Lions, the House of Dionysus mosaics, and the ancient theater with a private archaeologist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon at Super Paradise Beach — a stunning, more relaxed alternative to Paradise Beach, with clear turquoise water and a premium beach bar. Alternatively, visit Agios Sostis Beach for a quieter, more authentic experience.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Mykonos — enjoy the legendary Mykonos nightlife with cocktails at a rooftop bar before a farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up before the Delos excursion
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a taverna in Mykonos Town upon return from Delos — try M-eating (Kalogera 10) for elevated Greek cuisine in a chic setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Remezzo Restaurant (Chora, Mykonos) — a sophisticated waterfront restaurant with panoramic harbor views, serving premium Greek seafood and an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: Delos is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Ferries depart from the Old Port of Mykonos at 9:00 and 10:00 — arrive early. The site has no shade, so bring a hat, sunscreen, and water. The island has no permanent residents and no overnight stays are permitted.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Mykonos by high-speed ferry or short domestic flight to Zakynthos (Zante). The journey typically requires a connection via Athens or Patras — allow a full morning for travel. Check in to your luxury hotel on Zakynthos (recommended: Lesante Blu Exclusive Beach Resort or Porto Zante Villas & Spa).
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, visit the Blue Caves (Kianoun Spileon) on the northern tip of Zakynthos — a series of stunning sea caves where the water glows an ethereal electric blue due to light refraction. Accessible only by boat, this is one of Greece's most magical natural wonders. Arrange a private boat tour from your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) — rebuilt in Venetian style after the 1953 earthquake, with elegant arcaded streets, a beautiful main square (Plateia Solomou), and the impressive Byzantine Museum.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast in Mykonos before departure
meals.lunch: Light meal at the port or airport during transit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malanos Restaurant (Agios Nikolaos, Zakynthos) — a beloved local institution serving traditional Zakynthian cuisine including sofrito (veal in white wine sauce), bianco (fish in garlic sauce), and local wines

day_by_day.notes: The Mykonos–Zakynthos connection requires planning — check ferry and flight schedules carefully. A domestic flight via Athens (Mykonos–Athens–Zakynthos) is the most reliable option. Confirm hotel transfer from Zakynthos Airport.

day_by_day.morning: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit — The highlight of Zakynthos. Take a private or small-group boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of the most photographed beaches in the world. Enclosed by towering white limestone cliffs and accessible only by sea, the beach features the rusting wreck of the MV Panagiotis cargo ship half-buried in brilliant white sand, lapped by impossibly turquoise water. Swim, snorkel, and photograph this extraordinary natural spectacle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat tour to explore the sea caves and grottos along the western coastline of Zakynthos. Stop at secluded coves for swimming. Return to your hotel by mid-afternoon for relaxation at the pool or spa.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the clifftop viewpoint above Navagio Beach (accessible by road) — one of the most dramatic sunset vantage points in all of Greece.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — energize before the boat excursion
meals.lunch: Onboard the boat — arrange a catered lunch or stop at a seaside taverna in Porto Vromi (the departure point for Navagio boats) for fresh grilled fish
meals.dinner: Dinner at Zakanthi Restaurant (Kalamaki, Zakynthos) — an elegant garden restaurant serving refined Zakynthian and Mediterranean cuisine with an excellent local wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach can only be reached by boat — no road access. Book a private boat charter for the most exclusive experience (€200–€400 for a half-day). The beach can get crowded with tour boats mid-morning; aim to arrive before 10:00 or after 14:00. Bring snorkeling gear.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the KTEL Loggerhead Sea Turtle Conservation Center or take a guided tour of the National Marine Park of Zakynthos — the nesting ground of the endangered Caretta caretta loggerhead sea turtle. Zakynthos is one of the most important nesting sites in the Mediterranean. A guided eco-tour provides fascinating insight into conservation efforts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Venetian Castle (Kastro) of Zakynthos Town, perched on a pine-forested hill with panoramic views of the island and the Ionian Sea. Visit the Museum of Solomos and Eminent Zakynthians, dedicated to Dionysios Solomos, the poet who wrote the Greek national anthem. Spend the late afternoon at Gerakas Beach — a pristine protected beach and sea turtle nesting site.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening on Zakynthos — enjoy a leisurely stroll through Zakynthos Town and a farewell dinner celebrating the end of your Greek island journey.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with fresh local produce
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside taverna at Gerakas Beach — simple, fresh, and authentic Zakynthian cooking
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Prosilio Restaurant (Zakynthos Town) — a sophisticated restaurant in a beautifully restored building, offering creative Greek cuisine with premium local ingredients and an extensive Greek wine list

day_by_day.notes: Sea turtle nesting season runs May–October — respect all beach regulations (no lights, no umbrellas in marked nesting zones). The Venetian Castle is best visited in the late afternoon for golden-hour photography. Pack light for tomorrow's return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at your hotel. Take a final walk along the Zakynthos waterfront promenade, pick up last-minute souvenirs (local olive oil, Zakynthian mandolato nougat, local wine, and honey), and visit any remaining sights in Zakynthos Town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Zakynthos International Airport (Dionysios Solomos Airport) for your return flight. Depending on your departure time, connect via Athens International Airport for your Air Serbia return flight to Belgrade. Allow ample connection time at Athens (minimum 2.5 hours recommended for international connections).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Athens or in-transit — reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Greek beaches, world-class cuisine, ancient history, and island magic.

meals.breakfast: Final luxurious hotel breakfast — savor every last bite of Greek yogurt, local honey, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Zakynthos Airport or Athens Airport — try the premium lounges at Athens International Airport (Goldair Handling VIP Lounge or No1 Lounges)
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm all return flight details and connections the evening before. Allow extra time at Zakynthos Airport as it is a smaller regional airport. Consider purchasing premium Greek food products as gifts — vacuum-packed olives, extra virgin olive oil, and Greek honey travel well. Keep receipts for VAT refund eligibility on purchases over €50.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC
